intelligence.enrichment: Water vapour rises, cools, condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds, and many droplets together fall as rain, hail, or snow. Upward movement and cooling of water vapour cause condensation; growth and coming together of droplets leads to precipitation. The learner correctly applies this rule: Water vapour rises, cools, condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds, and many droplets together fall as rain, hail, or snow. Clouds are just invisible water vapour collected overhead, so droplets are not needed before rain.
